notes: DRAFT -- drafted by Claude from frame-by-frame inspection, NOT yet confirmed in the annotator. Keys carried in from t=1.1, held up to the camera t=1.6-3.6, lowered and set on the white desk at t=7.1; wearer walks to the kitchen (out of shot t=10.5-19.5) and returns to the same desk, keys still there t=20-25.2. Boundaries of the second in-shot range are the least certain part: at t=20-21 the desk is across the room and the keys are ~26 px on target, so whether they are 'in shot' is a judgement call -- check 198-215 and 245-255 first. Boxes are sparse by design; frames 95-100 and 245-250 have none, so no IoU is scored there. On the desk the keys measure 26-67 px on target at 720p, well below the ~128 px identity floor: this clip scores grounding and events, never identity. This clip's t_start is 0.1, so its windows end at t=7.1, 14.1 and 21.1, and the placement at t=7.1 lands EXACTLY on the first window's boundary (spans are `start < t <= end`) -- so window 1 counts it and the clip has two catchable placement windows instead of one. That is a knife-edge worth a reviewer's attention: t=7.1 is the first frame the keys rest on the desk, the hand is clear by t=7.6, and moving the event there costs the clip a window.
